conditions.tile: 40 x 40 nm single-layer square-lattice Rothemund sheet, 15 duplexes
conditions.element: C-0034's E5a on C-0039's inextensible two-spring elastica, free to draw in (H = 0), far anchorage A2 = the arm's own duplex end
conditions.maturity: TRL 1-3; nothing here is measured and the motif is not demonstrated

bounds.name: hinge count admitted at CH-0029's path-count floor
bounds.statement: n h <= 56 intersected with n >= 34 at the desired stroke leaves h = 1. Fewer paths are forbidden by the allowable and longer hinge lines by the inventory, so the trade has ONE admissible hinge count at the desired stroke, before any elastica runs

bounds.name: hinge-supplied arm ceiling, exact rotation [nm]
bounds.statement: the arm the WHOLE crossover inventory can place if the far anchorage carries nothing. A function of the PRODUCT n h and of nothing else, so it is CONSTANT along the whole trade curve — the degeneracy this task exists to test — and it is below §3's desired 10 nm stroke

bounds.name: the same at small rotation [nm]
bounds.statement: sqrt(N k_theta/k_target), the delta -> 0 limit, which the exact reading bounds from above

bounds.name: combined rigid-arm ceiling at 45 paths [nm]
bounds.statement: the same bound with C-0034's A2 anchorage restored: the restraint is N k_theta + n k_far, which grows with the PATH count. It is NOT degenerate, and it is what says which way the trade runs

bounds.name: combined rigid-arm ceiling at 56 paths [nm]
bounds.statement: and at the largest path count the inventory admits at h = 1

bounds.name: collinear interface supply [nm]
bounds.statement: 14 interior interfaces of a 15-duplex sheet plus its 2 free edges, at 40 nm each

bounds.name: the stroke C-0017's stability floor alone permits at 100 pN [nm]
bounds.statement: placement is k_c = F/delta and stability is k_c > |k_eff| = 23.41-27.91 pN/nm at the 10 nm layer in 2 mM, so the two together cap the stroke at 3.583-4.272 nm with no reference to what the coupling is made of

verdict.the trade is degenerate on its own axis: The hinge-supplied arm ceiling depends on the PRODUCT n h and on nothing else, so it is 5.387 nm at EVERY point of the n h = 56 trade curve — a flexure array cannot buy arm length by moving crossovers from one hinge to another. What is NOT degenerate is C-0034's far anchorage, whose couple is per-FLEXURE: the array's restraint is N k_theta + n k_far, so the placed arm GROWS with the path count and the trade runs OPPOSITE to the premise of the task. Fewer, longer flexures are strictly worse than more, shorter ones.
verdict.the desired stroke, at both readings of: P3 (the standing placement): 0 of 31 points at the WORKING-POINT reading and 0 of 31 at the WHOLE-STROKE reading. P10 (§3's own arithmetic for the desired clause): 0 and 0. The best point anywhere reaches 3.877 nm inside the ceiling. T-107's question does not move this verdict: the desired stroke fails at BOTH readings, and it fails on the geometry and the allowable before the ceiling is consulted.
verdict.why P10 is not an escape: Placing for §3's desired clause at its own force gives k_c = 10.000 pN/nm, which is 2.34-2.79x BELOW C-0017's stability floor at the 10 nm layer in 2 mM. Stability and placement together cap the stroke at 3.583-4.272 nm at 100 pN, with no reference to the coupling's construction at all.
verdict.what the branch DOES deliver: §3's ACCEPTABLE 3 nm stroke is met with margin: 3 points of the ledger-admitted sweep clear it, the best at 56 paths and 1 crossovers with a usable stroke of 3.312 nm, an arm of 9.973 nm = 29.3 bp and 1.786 pN per path against the 10 pN unzip allowable.
